$comment: One edit to seeded-correct-run: R-003 states a score of 5 where 3 x 2 is 6.
It is in the corpus because it pins the one thing about this document a parser can settle without any
judgment at all, and because it shows the two shape checks are independent claims that a single wrong
cell can violate together. The row breaks arithmetic, and 5 also falls outside the Score >=6 heading it
sits under, so it breaks band placement as well. Both are reported, because a reader fixing the row
needs to know the band moved with it.
The document is CONSTRUCTED, identical to seeded-correct-run apart from that one cell.
derivation: Everything seeded-correct-run derives holds except the two checks the edited cell touches.
Arithmetic: R-003 is 3 x 2, which is 6, and the row states 5. Both factors are still in 1..3, so the row
stays inside the denominator: inScale is 5, arithmeticTotal is 5, arithmeticOk falls to 4.
Band: R-003 sits under Score >=6 and now states 5, which the range does not contain, so bandOk falls to
4 over a banded count of 5.
Grounding is unchanged at 5 of 5: the description was not edited, and the scorer matches on the
description and the category, never on the score. Coverage is unchanged at 5 of 5 and all nine ordering
pairs still resolve and pass, because priority comes from the coverage plan, which was not edited.
WHAT MOVED AT SCORER VERSION 5
`banded` is now `rows` on every case, because a row under a heading that declares no score range is a
band failure rather than an exemption. `cleanControl` is `ceiling` and both sets declare one, so the
seeded corpus is bounded too. `grounding` carries `topSeverityMissed`, the count of the set's
lowest-ranked risks that went unreported. Material risks are assigned by maximum matching rather than
first-come, and every row is tested against the exclusions whether or not it matched a material risk.
AT SCORER VERSION 6
`ordering` carries `flattened`, which is true when every material risk that reached a priority reached
the same one. A plan like that satisfies every pairwise constraint without ordering anything, so the
metric reports unmeasurable rather than a perfect score.
AT SCORER VERSION 7
`unscoredRiskTables` records every table that names risks with an `R-NNN` id and states no score. Such a
table cannot be scored and used to be skipped without a word, so a register split across a scored table
and an unscored one lost its second half silently. The threshold on the count is zero.

shapeFailures.heading: High-Priority Risks (Score ≥6)
shapeFailures.reason: the score falls outside the range its heading declares
